explanation: An apostle who was a central figure in early Christianity and wrote several letters, including this letter about reconciliation.
The apostle Paul identifies himself as a servant of this person, who is the central figure in Christian belief in salvation.
A person who performs a service or task for someone else; here used to describe Paul's role under Jesus Christ.
In the context of this letter, the word refers to Paul, who wrote the letter while he was imprisoned because of his faith and preaching.
A Christian man from Colossae who owned a slave named Onesimus; the recipient of this letter's message about reconciliation.
The apostle Paul greets Appia, who was Philemon's wife or sister in the faith, and acknowledges her role in the local church.
The gathering of Christians that meets at Philemon's home; a community where believers come together to worship God.
